key_insight: Quantum-network fidelity estimation should use analytical computation, simulation, or learned surrogates according to the complexity of stochastic effects and online control needs.
engineering_relevance: Timely fidelity estimates can guide routing, scheduling, entanglement provisioning, purification, and quantum-memory allocation.
method: Compute fidelity analytically in simple regimes.
Simulate probabilistic entanglement generation, memory waiting times, and decoherence.
Train lightweight surrogates to approximate simulator outputs for online control.
evidence_signal: A simulation-based proof of concept shows that stochastic memory effects can require distribution-level fidelity estimates, while learned surrogates approximate simulator labels at much lower runtime cost.
watch_item: Deployment requires validation beyond simulator-generated labels, particularly for sim-to-real transfer and generalization to full network topologies.
paper_title: Quality-of-Transmission Estimation in Quantum Networks: Compute, Simulate, or Learn?
